summary.headline: KOEL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 16% to INR1,461 crore, but EBITDA fell 4% and margin contracted to 11.2% on commodity costs and export weakness.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,461 crore, led by domestic power gen (+18%), industrial (+19%) and distribution & aftermarket (+20%), while international fell 11% to INR106 crore. Standalone EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR165 crore and margin compressed to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributed to lower export volumes, elevated commodity costs and a lag between cost inflation and price realisation. Standalone net profit fell 9% to INR99 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR2,000 crore, with consolidated net profit down 17% to INR111 crore. Management said pricing actions have been taken across most businesses and expects profitability to improve as they flow through over coming quarters.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone net cash (net of debt, incl. treasury investments)

segments.name: Standalone power generation
segments.commentary: Revenue INR720 crore, +18% YoY; management cites sub-30 kVA portfolio redesign and domestic share gains, mainly below 750 kVA.

segments.name: Standalone industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue INR368 crore, +19% YoY; construction up double digits, marine up 125%, railways up 62%, plus first natural gas genset order from oil and gas (ONGC) up to 500 kVA.

segments.name: Standalone distribution & aftermarket
segments.commentary: Revenue INR268 crore, +20% YoY; growth across all channels led by service; 12 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth cited.

segments.name: Standalone international
segments.commentary: Revenue INR106 crore, -11% YoY; Middle East below normal levels due to West Asia conflict and logistics disruption.

segments.name: Consolidated B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,488 crore, +17% YoY; PBIT INR115 crore, -18% YoY.

segments.name: Consolidated B2C (KOEL Fluid Dynamics)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR301 crore, +3% YoY; PBIT INR26 crore, -7% YoY. Fluid Dynamics business broadly flat at INR294 crore; domestic up, exports down; channel pumps more than doubled.

segments.name: Financial services (Arka)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR210 crore, +9% YoY; PBT INR9 crore, -31% YoY; AUM INR7,651 crore; around 136 branches and over 1,800 employees.

guidance_outlook: Management says it remains committed to EBITDA delivery for the full year despite international headwinds.
Pricing actions taken across most businesses; realisation staged over different timeframes, expected to flow through over coming quarters.
Management views 3 to 6 months as a reasonable horizon for supply-chain queues and input-cost normalisation.
Long-term aspiration of a $2 billion revenue enterprise by FY30, roughly INR16,600 crore per management; no year-wise breakup given.
Management aims for a higher double-digit EBITDA margin by FY30 but declined to give a specific range; says margins have improved more than 400 bps over three years.
Data center order (~192 MW hyperscale): genset revenue to be recognised in FY27; O&M contract runs at least 5 to 6 years.
capex_capacity: First hyperscale data center order of approximately 192 MW secured in Q1, composite genset supply plus O&M contract.
NPCIL order is milestone-based; execution has started and some revenue expected this financial year; no NPCIL contribution in Q1.
Completed first end-to-end turnkey repowering of a 1,010 kVA high horsepower installation won in direct competition.
Optiprime modular power platform for data centers and mission-critical infrastructure; hybrid architectures up to 2 MW cited.
Largest range of CPCB IV compliant gas gensets claimed; new energy vertical is at programme-management stage (ethanol, methanol, isobutanol, natural gas, hydrogen).
Defense subsidiary Kirloskar Advanced Systems Limited established last quarter; no revenue contribution discussed.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand broad-based; management says market share gains are mostly below 750 kVA and only marginal above 750 kVA.
Pricing realisation varies by segment: power gen and distribution can pass on price readily, industrial and tenders are contract-specific, and fluid dynamics differs; realisation has lagged in Q1.
Middle East, a key export market, operated below normal levels due to West Asia conflict and choked logistics routes.
Management declined to split Power Gen growth between price and volume.
Employee cost rose about INR31 crore YoY (~40%), attributed to annual increments, ESOP expense, and capability additions; management says some costs are structural and some timing-related.
Inventory days rose slightly to 264 to support business expansion; cash conversion cycle at 25 days.

qa_highlights.question: Customer profile and further pipeline for the hyperscaler data center order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order is a reference point, not an endpoint, with one customer materialised through purchase orders after checks; further orders are proprietary and not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost jump roughly 40% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited a bridge of about INR31 crore YoY from increments, ESOP expense, and capability investments; some costs structural, some timing, not characterised as one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Has NPCIL or defence/marine revenue started?
qa_highlights.answer: No NPCIL contribution in Q1; execution milestone-based, revenue to start this FY. Defence and marine opportunities being pursued without specific Q1 contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Reasons for gross margin decline and pass-through of price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin contraction mainly from global commodity prices; price increases taken, with realisation lagging. Management says KOEL was among the first to start price conversations with customers.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for international business and normalisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Weakness mainly Middle East due to logistics disruption; management sees 3 to 6 months as a reasonable normalisation horizon as queues open.

qa_highlights.question: Is Arka being hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Arka CFO said a hive-off is the long-term plan, to be pursued in stepwise options, with updates to be shared when available.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin recovery depends on price realisation lagging cost inflation; watch Q2 margin trend.
Export and Middle East recovery timing; international revenue down 11% and operating leverage hit.
Employee cost run-rate (~40% YoY rise) against revenue; management promised fixed-cost absorption but gave no target.
Data center order execution, further order visibility, and customer experience in hyperscale segment; management declined to disclose pipeline.
Arka hive-off and segment PBT down 31% YoY; Fluid Dynamics export recovery.
Marine and railway growth described as partly execution and billing timing; sustainability uncertain.
